DDInter636.mechanism: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors may potentiate the hypotensive effects of diuretics and other antihypertensive agents or vasodilators. Volume depletion-related adverse reactions including hypotension, postural dizziness, orthostatic hypotension, syncope, and dehydration can occur after initiating treatment with SGLT-2 inhibitors, and the risk may be increased with concomitant use of other agents that can lower blood pressure.

DDInter638.mechanism: In patients without diabetes, coadministration of aliskiren with ACE inhibitors or ARBs may also be associated with increased risk of symptomatic hypotension, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function including acute renal failure. The risk of symptomatic hypotension is increased in the presence of marked volume and/or salt depletion. In patients with type 2 diabetes and renal impairment, coadministration of aliskiren with ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) has been associated with an increased risk of adverse events including renal complications, hyperkalemia, and hypotension.
